title: Exiled to Another World
text: “U-um? Would you like to make a bid?”
The monster merchant’s subordinate asked me. Well, I happened to have money on hand, indeed. Same as back when I picked up the egg that would become Rival.
“I’ll be taking this, but I’d ask you not to make a fuss about it, I say. Report it to that merchant over there later.”
“Y-yes… but that egg is—”
“Keep quiet about it. I’m paying plenty. Do you want to hinder future business, hm?”
“N-no…”
“Hmm? Whatcha doin’, Moto~?”
Ngh… Kuro-chan frowned at the egg in my hands.
“You gonna raise that one?”
“I won’t be raising it, indeed. But I can’t just leave it lying around.”
“Hmm…”
Satisfied that I wasn’t going to raise it, Kuro-chan nodded without further complaint. The Siltvelt envoy had been watching the whole exchange too, but didn’t seem inclined to say anything about it.
“Well then, since Father and the others’ negotiations seem to be wrapping up, Kuro-chan and I will go collect the Filolial-samas and rejoin Big Sister and the others.”
“Okay, let’s go, let’s go!”

Kuro-chan, apparently having sized up the place well enough, marched straight out of the tent. And so I rejoined Kuro-chan and the others at Big Sister’s side. After a while, we’d collect Father too and prepare for what came next. But before that, I quietly took the egg I’d picked up—the one that was surely destined to hatch into Rival—and warped away to a certain location via portal.
“No way it can reach me here, I say.”

The place I warped to was, of all places, the world where that Glass person resided. It seemed, from all the looping so far, that portal travel between worlds was possible. And as I vaguely recalled the Spirit of the Spear mentioning, this world apparently consisted of both our side and Glass’s side coexisting—so if I just dumped Rival’s egg over here, that thing would have no way of reaching our world. I warped to some spot I’d marked down during, what was it, that Filo-tan live tour thing, and hurled the egg into a nearby patch of grass.
“Go be a Demon King and duke it out with the reincarnators over here, I say! HAHAHAHAHA!”
This world is mine to leave in my hands, I say! You are entirely unnecessary here.
“This time, I will NOT hand Father over to you, indeed! FUHAHAHAHAHA!”

And so, the moment the portal’s cooldown ended, I leapt back through, laughing all the way. I did it, Father! Filo-tan! With this, Rival can’t reach us anymore! …And as I laughed, the image of Father getting stolen away by Rival flashed through my mind, and I couldn’t help but grimace.

What? You say Rival’s persistent enough to make it back to our world anyway? I wouldn’t know anything about that. I’ll simply make sure to solidify my footing so thoroughly that there’s no room left for it to wedge itself in, and make certain it never becomes one of our companions.
There’s no seat for you here! That’s the treatment it’s getting from me, indeed!

I will not hand over Father’s virtue to that thing. Before it ever arrives, Father needs to have found a proper partner, and quickly. I recall the Spirit of the Spear saying something about wanting me to “steal” Father away myself, but Father has expressed a wish for a normal, proper romance. Father as a married woman would be positively enchanting, I say!

Now then, time to bring out Yuki-chan and the others I’ve secured. I really must introduce them to Father. As for when to go fetch Fleon-chan… if I bring Kuro-chan and the others along, I imagine the Sage would happily cooperate. Either way, securing Fleon-chan is on the agenda soon. Once that’s done, she should be able to skillfully talk some sense into Itsuki, who’s been getting rather full of himself this loop. Speaking of which, memories of Itsuki from the previous loop, furiously protesting, surfaced in my mind.
‘If you don’t knock it off, I have my own methods too, you know. Just because you can loop doesn’t mean you get to do whatever you want.’

Something along those lines, if I recall correctly. He’d said to find some method other than awakening Fleon-chan’s sense of justice… A rather selfish request, if you ask me. Honestly, after the way he gleefully condemned Father last time while riding high on his own self-righteousness, I feel like anything I do to him would be justified—but, tedious as it is, I suppose I’ll show a bit of consideration. That “other method” the Spirit of the Spear mentioned, I believe. Though… what a bother. I’ll leave Itsuki alone for now.
“Welcome back, Motoyasu-kun.”
After discarding Rival and bringing out Yuki-chan and the others’ eggs, I rejoined Father and the others, and Father came out to greet me.
“I’m back.”
“Oh? A new Filolial egg? You’re still collecting more even though you already have some?”
“Indeed I am. Starting from this loop, counting forward to the next, I’ve gone and secured Yuki-chan and the others—Filolial-samas who’ll be lending us their strength.”
“Huh. Like, regulars or something?”

“Just so. If I miss the timing, they sometimes end up shipped off elsewhere, I say. This egg here is the one that becomes Yuki-chan. Though there’s another possibility where she becomes White Swan instead.”

Kou never gets shipped off—stays right there at the Filolial breeder’s place under safekeeping—but Yuki-chan and Sakura-chan do end up shipped away. Yuki-chan, being a thoroughbred, becomes White Swan as a racehorse. White Swan being simply another possible form Yuki-chan can take, you see.
“The name’s different though…”

“White Swan is the form she takes when raised as a racing bird on a ranch, indeed. Same as how Kuro-chan becomes Black Thunder, true name Kurotaro—her temperament turns considerably more fierce in that case.”
“Really? Kuro-chan’s supposed to be a boy, but she seems more like a girl now—is that one of the differences too?”
“Just so. Black Thunder was a boy, indeed.”
Same sort of shift as between Kuro-chan and Black Thunder.
“So then, um… is Yuki-chan a boy too, maybe?”
Oh my? It seems Father had been picturing Yuki-chan as a boy this whole time.
“Yuki-chan is a girl, I say. Though if Father would prefer, I could raise her as a boy—like with Keel.”
“Who’s Keel? Anyway, forget that—you don’t need to raise her like some troubled parent trying to force something. Also, why does Kuro-chan get a ‘chan’ attached?”
“She herself requested to be addressed with ‘chan,’ so that’s how I address her, indeed.”
Just so. Kuro-chan wished to be called with the “chan” suffix. Hence I call her Kuro-chan. Though Kuro-chan herself refers to herself simply as Kuro.
“Well then, I’ll let Yuki-chan grow up freely as Yuki-chan.”

I had considered, for variety’s sake, not securing Yuki-chan now and instead scouting her later as White Swan… but Yuki-chan’s leadership qualities are far too reliable to pass up, so I’d rather secure her early. There are certainly other Filolial-samas who grow up to be reliable too, but Yuki-chan is by far the safest bet. Chick and Midori from the very first world tend to vary too much between worlds in that regard—too difficult to reproduce reliably. Which naturally makes Yuki-chan the best fit for the role of leader.
“I’d like to have Yuki-chan take charge of directing the other Filolials, I say.”
“Can’t Kuro-chan do that instead?”
Father’s question, indeed.
“Kuro-chan is decent enough at looking after others, but in that case, there’s a real risk all the Filolial-samas raised under her end up picking up Kuro-chan’s particular manner of speech, I say.”

If I recall what Father said during the loop where we reunited with Fleon-chan, it was something about “chuunibyou contamination.” Same as with Black Thunder—Kuro-chan carries that same factor, so making her the dedicated leader wouldn’t really be advisable. Leaving it to Fleon-chan carries similar risks too, come to think of it.
